newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Berner withdraws from Spain, omits dividend.
newsitem.headline: Berner withdraws from Spain, omits dividend.

text.p: Swiss insurer Berner Holding AG, the parent company of the Berner Group, said it planned to take provisions of 44.1 million Swiss francs to divest itself of its activities in Spain, leading to a loss of 26.0 million Swiss francs in the 1996/97 financial year.
The holding company's board of directors would therefore propose to omit a dividend, Berner Holding said in a statement.

Berner, in which German insurance group Allianz Holding AG holds a majority stake, said its board had decided to withdraw from the loss-making Spanish insurance group Amaya, jointly owned by Waadt Insurance.
Berner said that a turnaround in Amaya would only be possible with considerable investments, but neither it nor Waadt were prepared to take that step.
Although details of the withdrawal have not been finalised, Berner said it had fully written off its participation in Amaya and precautionary provisions of 44.1 million francs were taken.

"Despite participation income from the Swiss subsidiaries within the expected range, the annual result of Berner Holding will end with a yearly loss of 26 million francs due to these extraordinary burdens," Berner said.
Combined with the profit from last year, this results in a balance sheet loss of 23.3 million francs, which will be financed through special reserves.
"The board of directors considers this radical move indispensable," the company said.
In the future, Berner will focus on its core business in Switzerland and strengthen its position as a quality insurer for private customers, as well as small and medium-sized companies.
